source_user: A service receives a mix of short prompts and long generations. Design an evaluation plan that reports TTFT, TPOT, throughput, queueing, and P99 latency. Scenario variant 91: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: separate prefill and decode behavior; fix workload distribution; report warmup; use repeated trials; capture GPU memory and request-level traces.
corrected_answer: For scenario variant 91: Freeze and record model/tokenizer, runtime and kernel versions, hardware topology, precision, parallelism, scheduler/batching, sampling, arrival process, prompt/output-length distributions, offered loads, concurrency, SLOs, and correctness criteria; conclusions are limited to this configuration. Hypothesis: at each prespecified offered load, candidate B changes paired TTFT, TPOT, queue wait, throughput, or P99 latency versus baseline A by a predefined practically meaningful effect, without unacceptable correctness, timeout, cancellation, or error-rate regression. Pre-register effect thresholds, uncertainty rule, sample size or stopping rule, exclusions, and missing-data handling. Replay the same fixed, stratified request trace with randomized A/B order and repeated independent time blocks on equivalent isolated hosts; document and exclude only warm-up. Capture admission, queue entry/exit, dispatch, prefill start/end, first-token, each decode-token, completion, cancellation, timeout, retry, error, and rejection timestamps. Report queue-inclusive and compute-only TTFT, define TPOT denominator (decode time divided by generated tokens, with zero-token cases handled), end-to-end latency, request/token throughput, queue wait, and P50/P95/P99 by workload stratum and offered load. Include bootstrap or block-level uncertainty and denominators; report correctness, truncation, timeout, cancellation, and error rates. Collect GPU memory, utilization, power, clocks, temperature, CPU, host memory, KV-cache occupancy/evictions, batch sizes, and throttling, and log version/config hashes. Investigate warm-cache effects, co-tenancy, thermal drift, trace imbalance, retries, scheduler adaptation, and host/network noise with randomized blocks and matched baselines. Treat missing telemetry as a limitation, not as success. Require independent replay and artifact review before claiming a result; if correctness or safety limits fail, or tail latency exceeds the rollback guardrail, stop rollout and revert to A. All numerical claims require measured traces; estimates must state units and assumptions.
risks: No platform-specific facts or measured benchmark values are available.
P99 estimates can be unstable under sparse tails or nonstationary load.
Instrumentation and replay may perturb queueing and cache behavior.
evidence_required: Versioned configuration and deployment manifest.
Request-level trace with queue/prefill/decode timestamps and token counts.
Repeated randomized paired runs with uncertainty intervals and correctness/error denominators.
GPU/CPU/cache/thermal telemetry and independent artifact review.
